title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming stability, function/tool-calling, roles/stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Asha Patel
description: This PR brings our OpenAI compatibility layer closer to /v1/chat.completions parity by addressing several API surface gaps: more stable streaming behavior for tools/function-calls, explicit support for roles and stop sequences when returning token-level logprobs, and improved response formatting to match OpenAI edge cases. Motivation: customers using our OpenAI compatibility endpoint observed differences in streaming event ordering and structured output around function/tool calls, and some SDKs depend on exact key names/ordering for stop/logprobs fields. This change unifies behavior across runtime and SDKs, fixes flakiness seen in long streaming sessions, and adds regression tests. Scope: runtime streaming reordering fix, compatibility shim for function calls (name/arguments shape), explicit handling for multiple stop sequences and token logprob mappings, response formatter changes to match OpenAI's prioritization of 'choices' ordering and 'finish_reason' semantics. See linked Linear tickets for more context.

b7c9e11: compat: emit function_call objects with (name,args) shape for openai compat layer (openai_compat.go)
c4d6a5e: response: normalize choices ordering and map finish_reason values (formatter.go)
d2e8f3b: api: accept list-of-stop sequences and prefer exact-match stop handling (compat layer)
e9f0a22: tests: add parity integration tests for streaming function calls and stop/logprobs (chat_parity_test.go)
f3a7d44: sdk/python: update openai compatibility helpers to expect function_call.name and arguments string (openai_compat.py)
review_comments: Miguel Santos: Could you add a short note on how this interacts with our prefix caching when streaming? We saw weird behavior when cache hits occur mid-stream.
Asha Patel: Addressed in stream_manager.go - we now flush cached prefixes as a preamble event to keep ordering consistent. Added test case to ensure prefix flush before function_call event.
Renee Zhao: A couple of nits on openai_compat.go naming, but overall LGTM. Please add release notes.
Daniel Kim: CI flake in chat_parity_test.go on first run; looks like a race in test harness. Added retry and explicit shutdown ordering.
ci_notes: Initial run: 1 flaky integration test failed (chat_parity_test.go) due to test harness race; rerun passed. All pipelines green (unit, integration, lint, e2e-staging).
release_notes: Improve OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: stabilize streaming order, support function/tool calling shape, handle roles and multiple stop sequences for token-level logprobs, and normalize response formatting to match OpenAI finish_reason semantics. Backwards compatible; minor SDK tweak for function_call argument shape.
notes_for_release_manager: This is a compatibility-forward change that could affect customers relying on earlier non-standard event ordering during streaming. Recommend a short entry in the changelog and a jira notification to customers on dedicated/private deployments. Rollout: main->release canary; no DB migrations.
testing_summary: Added integration tests that exercise long-running streaming sessions with function calls and multiple stop sequences. Added unit tests for response formatter mapping of finish_reason and token logprob shape. CI ran full suite and a flaky integration test was retried and passed.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: changes touch streaming core and compatibility layer. We exercised canary and e2e-staging. No data migrations. Monitoring: added a new alert for increased streaming event reorder rate and increased 'openai-compat' 5xx counts.
